{{Short description|Type of random variable}}
{{more footnotes|date=September 2025}}

In [[mathematics]], particularly in [[probability theory]] and [[stochastic geometry]], a '''random closed set''' is a [[random variable]] whose values are [[Closed set|closed subsets]] of a given [[topological space]], typically [[Euclidean space]] <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math>. Random closed sets generalize the concept of random variables and random processes by allowing entire [[Set (mathematics)|sets]], rather than individual points or [[Vector (mathematics and physics)|vectors]], to be treated as random elements. They are widely used in areas such as [[spatial statistics]], [[image analysis]], [[materials science]], and [[mathematical morphology]].

==Definition==
A random closed set in <math>\mathbb{R}^d</math> is a [[measurable function]] from a [[probability space]] <math>(\Omega,\mathcal{A}, P)</math> into <math>(\mathcal{F}, \Sigma)</math>. Here <math>\mathcal{F}</math> is the collection of all closed subsets of <math>\mathbb{R}^d</math> and <math>\Sigma</math> is the [[sigma-algebra]] generated over <math>\mathcal{F}</math> by the sets <math display="block">\mathcal{F}_K=\{F\in\mathcal{F}:F\cap K=\emptyset\}</math> for all [[Compact space|compact]] subsets <math>K\subset\mathbb{R}^d</math>.

==History==
Mentions of random sets have appeared for almost a century beginning with [[Andrey Kolmogorov|A.N. Kolmogorov's]] book, ''Foundations of the Theory of Probability'', which provided the axiomatic foundation for probability theory. In this book, Kolmogorov defined what is now referred to as a random set.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Kolmogorov |first1=A.N. |title=Foundations of the Theory of Probability |date=1950 |publisher=Chelsea Publishing Co. |isbn=978-1614275145 |url=https://psycnet.apa.org/record/1951-02753-000 |access-date=14 February 2025 |language=English |format=Print}}</ref> Up until the 1960s, mentions of random sets could be found scattered throughout publications before [[Gustave Choquet]] formalized the concept of a random set. French mathematician [[Georges Matheron]] is recognized as the first person to concentrate on random sets with ''closed'' values and formulate a definition.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Matheron |first1=Georges |title=Random Sets and Integral Geometry |journal=Royal Statistical Society |date=March 1976 |volume=139 |issue=2 |pages=277–278 |doi=10.2307/2345196 |url=https://academic.oup.com/jrsssa/article/139/2/277/7104782 |access-date=14 February 2025 |publisher=Wiley |jstor=2345196 |format=Print|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
